To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
photooxidative stress induced in the leaves of orange trees results in the modulation of the metabolism of nearby fruit pulp.
photooxidative stress signals propagate to nearby organs in citrus, and that the quality of fruits is affected by the signals.

(i) photooxidative stress induces the expression of genes involved in the AA/GSH cycle and the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in leaves, and (ii) this signal is propagated to nearby fruits where it affects the activities of the AA/GSH system, and the contents of sugars and carotenoids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of plant stress tolerance and adaptation to environmental stress.
the study of the mechanisms of stress perception, signal transduction and acclimation in plants.
the question of how plants can sense and respond to stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photooxidative damage in the leaves of citrus trees is transmitted to nearby fruits and affects their metabolism, which in turn affects the quality of the fruit.
the stress signals generated in leaves in response to photooxidative conditions may be transmitted to nearby fruits and influence their metabolism.
the metabolic response of the fruit to photooxidative leaf stress is a complex process, which may involve a combination of both systemic signalling and direct stress effects on the fruit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leaves submitted to oxidative stress can influence the metabolism in the nearby fruits.
the quality of orange fruits can be improved by photo-oxidative stress in leaves, and this is a novel approach to the management of quality criteria.
leaves are the first responders in photooxidative stress and that they are the first to be damaged.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality criteria in fruits are influenced by photooxidative signals in leaves.
the quality of fruits is not only driven by the fruit metabolism itself, but also by the metabolism of leaves.
leaves submitted to stress can affect fruit quality.
